To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the use of a novel, ultrapure dialysis fluid (UPDF) in patients undergoing chronic maintenance hemodialysis (HD) is associated with a significant improvement in the clinical and laboratory parameters of uremia, including a reduction of mortality.

1) the use of ultrapure dialysis fluid is safe and feasible in the clinical setting; 2) it is associated with improved patient survival, reduced hospitalization, and better dialysis tolerance; 3) the use of a dialysis fluid with a bacterial endotoxin content < 0.03 EU/mL is associated with a 50% reduction in the incidence of bacteremia; and 4) ultrapure dialysate is a safe and feasible option for the

(i) the dialysate used for hemodialysis (HD) is an essential component of the HD treatment; (ii) the use of ultrapure dialysate is associated with improved clinical outcomes in patients on maintenance HD; and (iii) the use of a bicarbonate-buffered, ultrapure dialysis fluid is a new standard for contemporary hemodialysis.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the structure and dynamics of the interfacial region between a liquid phase and a solid surface in the presence of an electric field.
the study of the structure and dynamics of complex fluids, such as colloidal dispersions and polymer solutions.
the development of new methods and materials for the purification of dialysate.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the current dialysis practice is far from optimal and that there is an urgent need to improve the quality of care for dialysis patients.
there are many reasons to use ultrapure dialysis fluids.
dialysates with a high biocompatibility profile are associated with a better clinical outcome in patients on maintenance hemodialysis.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
it was a collaborative and interdisciplinary effort to develop and implement a novel dialysis fluid that would be safe and efficacious for patients undergoing dialysis therapy.
the dialysis fluid used in contemporary dialysis is far from being a mere vehicle for the transport of toxins from the blood into the dialysis fluid compartment.
the current standards of care for hemodialysis patients have been established based on the results of clinical trials conducted over the past 2 decades.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we should not be content with the status quo.
the use of ultrapure dialysis fluid (UPDF) is safe and effective in patients with chronic kidney disease.
the current dialysate standard is not good enough, and that a better dialysis fluid can be developed and should be developed.
